provenance_coverage.granularity: scenario-level: 3 activities, generated_entity points at the scenario bundle, not at individual records

platform_state_not_used_for_review.rule: review_status comes only from fold(review-event ledger) (§4 A3)

disclosures.title: Evidence records carry no validity time; only capture time
disclosures.detail: claim-record has valid_time{start,end,description}; evidence-record has none. The engine can express when a quote was captured (captured_at) and when the source was published (source.published_at), but not the interval in which the quoted statement held. Any 'as valid at t' query over evidence is therefore UNKNOWN, not false.
disclosures.disposition: disclosed; requires contract change to close
disclosures.measured_by: lib.bitemporal() -> valid_time_resolution=not-applicable for all evidence rows

disclosures.title: Excerpts are elided; no character offsets, so no verbatim span is recoverable
disclosures.detail: 3/8 quotes contain ellipsis markers and 0/8 locators carry start_offset. The engine stores quote_sha256 of the *as-captured* excerpt only; it cannot re-verify the excerpt against the live source, and 'direct-quotation' must be read as 'stamped excerpt'.
disclosures.disposition: disclosed; retrieval surfaces quote_elided=true so no client mistakes it for a contiguous span

disclosures.title: Producer identity is fragmented across two id spellings
disclosures.detail: claims/evidence record created_by='claude-code-session-6f76cd3d (...)' while the provenance records name the same session 'cc-session-6f76cd3d' (external_id bg-job-6f76cd3d). A string-equality self-approval check would not fire on the alias. Engine therefore resolves identity by shared session token and fails closed (§4 A2).
disclosures.disposition: mitigated in v0.1 by token-based alias resolution + fail-closed rule; a durable identity registry (ke.identity_alias) is required before multi-agent approval

disclosures.title: Tool versions are unresolvable in provenance
disclosures.detail: 9/9 software entries have an empty version string. provenance-record allows it, but the engine cannot pin which tool build produced an artifact, so reproducibility claims must stay qualified.

disclosures.title: Provenance is scenario-level, not record-level
disclosures.detail: 12 records are reachable as activity used_entities (12 covered), but each of the 3 activities declares generated_entity = the scenario bundle. A per-record 'which activity generated *this* claim' answer is only derivable through used_entities membership, which also lists sources and unrelated ids.
disclosures.disposition: disclosed; acceptable for a 3-activity pilot, insufficient at record granularity

disclosures.title: Recorded epistemic_status exceeds the conservative cap on some claims
disclosures.detail: policy table T-5.2 caps a claim whose supporting evidence is anchored but unassessed (capture>=2, assessment_status=unassessed) at 'provisional'. Flagged: [('tkc:fair:a1-protocol-conditions', 'well-supported', 'provisional'), ('tkc:prov-o:wasattributedto-signature', 'established', 'provisional')]. The recorded value is preserved verbatim (never rewritten by the engine) and the computed cap is stored next to it for a reviewer to rule on.
disclosures.disposition: flag-only, non-destructive: engine never downgrades authored status; requires a review event to change it

disclosures.title: Validity intervals are prose-only for most claims
disclosures.detail: 2/4 claims describe validity in prose without start/end. The engine stores the prose and marks resolution=prose-only; it must NOT parse dates out of the prose (that would fabricate timestamps).
disclosures.disposition: disclosed; 'as valid at t' returns these claims as unknown-validity, not as false

disclosures.title: KO aggregates link claims through an open-vocabulary relations list
disclosures.detail: 3/3 KO elements use relations[{relation_type,target_id}] instead of the schema-sanctioned claim_refs/evidence_refs fields (0 uses of claim_refs). relation_type is free text, so the engine normalizes 4 observed tokens to a closed enum and keeps relation_type_raw on the edge. Support *direction* is taken from the token verb only.
disclosures.disposition: disclosed; closed-enum mapping table is part of this spec (KO_EDGE_MAP)

disclosures.title: No review events exist; review_status is a fold of an empty ledger
disclosures.detail: 0 review-event records exist in the pilot. Every entity's review_status='draft' therefore comes from fold(empty) by convention, not from a field — claim/evidence/provenance contracts have no review_status column at all. 'Not reviewed' must never be rendered as 'approved'.

disclosures.title: not-assessed is explicit for exactly one claim and is not the same as missing
disclosures.detail: tkc:tkrepo:rocrate-export-production is not-assessed because its only non-contextual evidence is a 'mentions' row in an internal planning table (insufficient). The engine stores this as an explicit status + insufficiency reasons, and rejects ingest of a claim whose status field is absent (absent != not-assessed).
disclosures.disposition: encoded as retrieval flag NOT_ASSESSED_EXPLICIT + insufficiency block

disclosures.title: Source published_at is a date, not an instant
disclosures.detail: evidence.source.published_at values are ISO dates (2013-04-30, 2026-06-22). The engine normalizes to midnight UTC and records precision='date'; the instant is a representation artifact, not a finding about the source.
disclosures.disposition: precision documented in the projection slot

audit.acceptance: no unreported loss: every leaf path is projected, and every semantic loss is listed in disclosures[]
